project.name: The Manhattan Project: The Secret Race to Build the Atomic Bomb
project.visual_rule: original programmatic historical diagrams and archival-document-style still reconstructions; no stock video clips and no fabricated archival photographs

scenes.title: The Weapon That Changed the World
scenes.caption: A secret wartime project with consequences beyond the war

scenes.title: A Discovery Inside the Atom
scenes.caption: Nuclear fission transformed theoretical physics into a possible weapon

scenes.title: The Warning to Roosevelt
scenes.caption: The Einstein–Szilard letter urged attention to the possibility of an atomic weapon

scenes.title: A Race Against Nazi Germany
scenes.caption: World war accelerated the effort to turn nuclear science into a weapon

scenes.title: The Manhattan Engineer District
scenes.caption: A vast federal program assembled scientists, engineers, factories and military command

scenes.title: The First Controlled Chain Reaction
scenes.caption: Enrico Fermi's Chicago Pile-1 demonstrated a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction

scenes.title: Oak Ridge: Uranium
scenes.caption: Industrial-scale uranium enrichment supplied material for the uranium weapon

scenes.title: Hanford: Plutonium
scenes.caption: Reactors and chemical separation facilities produced plutonium

scenes.title: Los Alamos: Designing the Bomb
scenes.caption: A remote laboratory brought scientists together to design the weapons

scenes.title: Oppenheimer and Groves
scenes.caption: Scientific leadership and military command coordinated an unprecedented undertaking

scenes.title: Trinity: The First Nuclear Explosion
scenes.caption: The plutonium implosion device was detonated in the New Mexico desert

scenes.title: Hiroshima
scenes.caption: The uranium bomb known as Little Boy was used against Hiroshima

scenes.title: Nagasaki
scenes.caption: The plutonium implosion bomb Fat Man was used against Nagasaki

scenes.title: The Nuclear Age Begins
scenes.caption: The project ended as a wartime program, but its scientific and ethical consequences endured
